correctness.rationale: The exact Binet identity B_{3t}=32B_t³+3B_t and symmetric geometric sums supply the polynomial identity 7*sum_{j=1}^{2m-1}B_{n+j}³=g[(4g²+3)B_{n+m}³+3(g²-1)B_{n+m}/8]. The parity recurrence for g (odd, g²≡1 mod16) makes H=3(g²-1)/8 integral. The balancing residues mod7 cycle 0,1,-1 and g residues 1,0,-1, making f_g(B_s) divisible by seven for all s. Explicit f_g(1)=7(5g²+3)/8 has exactly one factor of seven and no factors 2,3,5; if any p>=11 divided both f_g(1) and f_g(6), the differences would give p|A,H, contrary to 3A−32H=21. Thus gcd(f_g(1),f_g(6))=7. The companion recurrence matrix has determinant1 modulo every d, so its orbit is purely periodic: any common divisor of all tail polynomial values must divide the two initial values modulo d. Hence tail gcd exactly7, and cancelling the 7-factor in the whole-window identity gives g for all n>=0, not merely samples. Fresh independent exact arithmetic checked 12 odd lengths through k=23 at 23 starting indices each, verified the identity, primitive gcd and exponent-7 k=3 counterexample49.
